newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares slip despite diversified trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares slip despite diversified trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices slipped on Tuesday despite strong trade in a range of sectors.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index fell 0.42 points to 386.77 in average volume of 58.04 million pounds ($17.10 million).
"Trade was more diversified today. People are looking away from the more usual sectors, looking for hidden hot deals," said Mohammed Abdullah of Intercapital brokerage.
Commercial International Bank was the day's most actively-traded share, but it shed 0.23 pounds to close at 78.2 after shares worth more than eight million pounds changed hands.
"The bank's GDR is not doing too well and this is having an effect on its performance in Cairo. But I think it will stabilise at this price and soon pull up," Abdullah said.

Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries was the second most traded stock in Tuesday's market, closing one pound higher at 211 after shares worth more than 5.50 million pounds changed hands.
Abdullah predicted a promising future for the pharmaceutical sector, saying it may take over from mills as a favourite.
"Eipico is the best in the pharmaceutical sector, which has the lowest price-to-earning ratio on the market. The company has a lot of potential in terms of growth. It rarely loses."

Alexandria Pharmaceuticals and Chemical Industries closed unchanged at 127 after almost two million pounds were traded in the stock, while Memphis Pharmaceuticals and Chemical Industries closed 0.21 pounds higher at 81.7.
Paints and Chemical Industries/PACHIN performed well, gaining three pounds to close at 141. Abdullah said a forthcoming global depositary receipt had boosted interest in the stock.
Suez Cement, which Abdullah said is usually the quietest of the cements, closed 0.01 pounds higher at 72.01 after shares worth more than three million pounds were traded.

Abdullah said market rumours that a foreign investor was interested in buying Delta Insurance and Mohandes Insurance and merging the two into a joint venture had helped Delta's performance on Tuesday. The stock closed 1.50 higher at 31.5 pounds.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 584.41 from 590.16 points on Monday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 271.27 from to 270.19.
Of the 94 shares traded, 29 rose, 34 declined and 31 remained unchanged.
